Coach was an alumnus of Manchester High School Central, having lived in Manchester all his life.  Coach would then go on to Phillips Exeter Academy and Keene State College.  He began working at Hollis/Brookline in 1962 and started the cross-country, winter track, and spring track programs.  During his career, Coach led the Hollis/Brookline Cavaliers to twenty-six state championships.

Asemota found late interest in football during his sophomore year when a football coach approached him during a track meet because of his outstanding blend of height and speed.  The same coach, Calvin Taylor, then had Asemota playing wide receiver and free safety for him that season in 2014.

He also coached at Reed City High School, Rockford High School, and Hastings High School in Michigan.  The outdoor track at Central Michigan University is named for Bennett.

Courtney was fired from Texas Southern University on July 19, 2007.

After graduating from Somerville High School, Mahoney played running back for Holy Cross.  Before coming to Boston College, Mahoney coached high school football in the state of Massachusetts, first at Boston College High School (1910), and then at Somerville High School (1911–1913).  After two seasons as the head coach of the Boston College Eagles football team, Mahoney was replaced by the popular Charles Brickley and Mahoney returned to Somerville High to coach track.  He later served as a football official and as a city official in Cambridge, Massachusetts.  Mahoney served Cambridge's physical director, superintendent of the recreation, and director of athletics.
